manifest.name: dsh-desktop-notify
manifest.description: Desktop notifications for DeepSeek Harness: a Windows toast when a Session needs your approval or answer, or finishes a long run, with click-through back to that Session

bundle.text:
# dsh-desktop-notify bundle patch.
#
# One insert mounts the Host row the browser half binds to. The Host half
# registers nothing (see index.js): all notification work happens in the
# renderer, because that is the only process holding an AppUserModelID.
# package.json's `dsh.client` declares the browser half against this row.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-desktop-notify
      name: 'dsh-desktop-notify'

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Desktop notifications for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).
A Windows toast appears when a Session needs you — and clicking it brings that
Session back to the front.

Two triggers:

| Trigger | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs attention** | The Agent is blocked waiting for your approval or your answer. |
| **Run finished** | A Session that was running has stopped, and the run lasted at least `minRunMs`. |

Requires the **Desktop** application (the Windows toast path depends on Electron
running the renderer; a browser tab has no AppUserModelID to notify under).

readme.section: From the DSH plugin page (no terminal)
readme.text:
Open **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, and paste one of these into
**Package name or address**:

| What you paste | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| `github:guanhaisen/dsh-desktop-notify` | Straight from this repository. Nothing published to npm. |
| `https://github.com/guanhaisen/dsh-desktop-notify` | Same thing, written as a URL. |
| `D:\path\to\dsh-desktop-notify` | A local checkout. **Must be an absolute path.** |

readme.section: From the DSH plugin page (no terminal)
readme.text:
Then press **Install**. The plugin manager runs `pnpm add` in your profile, adds
the bundle to the profile's list, and the notification half activates without a
restart in most cases — reload the page (`Ctrl+R`) if the first toast does not
arrive.

> Installing from git resolves the repository's **default branch**. If you fork
> this and your default branch differs, paste the full spec with a ref instead:
> `github:you/dsh-desktop-notify#main`.

readme.section: From the DSH plugin page (no terminal)
readme.text:
> The plugin page states that installed plugins **do not auto-update**: to
> upgrade, uninstall and install again. A `github:` install follows the default
> branch, so reinstalling picks up new commits.
```bash

> Keep this package free of runtime `dependencies`. pnpm does not install a
> linked package's own dependencies, and a resolution failure during Cordis tree
> initialisation stops DSH from starting.

readme.section: You will not see a toast when…
readme.text:
| Situation | Why it is silent |
| --- | --- |
| You are looking at that Session | The prompt is already on screen. |
| The run was shorter than `minRunMs` (20 s) | A quick reply is not news. |
| The Session was already running when the window opened | The first snapshot is a baseline, so opening DSH does not fire a burst. |
| Windows **Do Not Disturb** is on | The OS suppresses the banner. The notification still reaches the notification centre. |

readme.section: You will not see a toast when…
readme.text:
If none of those apply and nothing appears, read the decision log — see
[Verifying it actually works](#verifying-it-actually-works). It records every
suppression *with its reason*, so "why did I not get a toast?" is answerable.

readme.section: Why this is a plugin and not a shell patch
readme.text:
The obvious implementation — add a `Notification` call to the Electron main
process — cannot work here, and understanding why explains the whole design.

The Desktop Host is **not** the Electron main process. `lib/main.js` spawns it as
a *separate Node child process*:

```js
spawn(this.node, ['--expose-internals', entry, ...], { stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe','ipc'] })
```

readme.section: Why this is a plugin and not a shell patch
readme.text:
That child is the Electron executable re-entered in Node mode, so
`require('electron')` inside a Host plugin yields no `Notification`, and the
process holds no AppUserModelID. Meanwhile the shell's own notification code
(`lib/main.js`) only ever fires for one thing: a mandatory update.

The renderer, however, has everything needed:

readme.section: Why this is a plugin and not a shell patch
readme.text:
- `dsh-app:` is registered as a privileged scheme with `standard: true` and
  `secure: true`, making the window a **secure context**, which the Web
  Notification API requires.
- The application session installs a permission handler that returns `true` for
  every non-media permission.

readme.section: Why this is a plugin and not a shell patch
readme.text:
So a plain Web `Notification` in the window becomes a real Windows toast under
the application's own identity (`electron.app.DeepSeek Harness`). No shell
patch, no helper process, and it survives application updates.

Nothing is polled and no second source of truth is created.
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` already folds exactly these facts and
publishes them as `ctx.uiSession.sessionStatus`:

```
Map<sessionId, { running, pendingInteraction, completionUnread }>
```

It is fed by the `api-session/status` Remote event. This plugin only reads it.

`pendingInteraction` is the interaction object itself, whose `kind` is one of:

| `kind` | Raised by | Copy shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `approval` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-approval` | Tool named in the request is asking for privileged execution |
| `question` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-user-questions` | The Agent asked a question |
| `plan-review` | same, when the questions are a plan | A plan is waiting for review |

Its `key` is the identity used to de-duplicate, so a status re-emission for the
same wait never produces a second toast.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Host half. Owns the Loader row the browser half binds to. Registers nothing — no tool, no service, no route. |
| `client.js` | Browser half. Watches Session status, decides when to notify, renders the toast, wires click-through, and publishes the `DesktopNotify` Inspect provider. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The one Host row the bundle inserts. |
| `test/watcher.test.mjs` | Behavioural test of the decision logic, runnable with plain `node`. |

Set on the plugin's row in the profile patch, or via the Plugins page:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `notifyOnAttention` | `true` | Notify when a Session is blocked on you. |
| `notifyOnComplete` | `true` | Notify when a run finishes. |
| `minRunMs` | `20000` | Ignore runs shorter than this. Quick replies are not news. |
| `sound` | `true` | Play the system notification sound. |

A repeated interaction never re-notifies: identity is the interaction's own
`key`, so a status re-emission for the same pending approval stays silent. The
first snapshot after the window opens is treated as a baseline rather than as
news, which is what stops a launch from firing a burst of toasts for Sessions
that were already running.

Delivery is asynchronous and visual, and neither half can observe the toast the
operating system renders. So the browser half publishes a Cordis Inspect
provider, `DesktopNotify`, which can be queried from outside the page:

| Method | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Is the half mounted? What is `Notification.permission`? Is this a secure context? Which Sessions are tracked, and since when? |
| `testToast` | Fire one real toast now, and report what was constructed. |
| `decisions` | The in-memory decision log — every notification sent *and* every one deliberately suppressed, with the reason. |

`decisions` is the one that answers "why did I not get a toast?": a suppressed
entry carries `suppressed: 'watched'` (you were looking at that Session) or
`suppressed: 'too-short'` (the run ended before `minRunMs`).

The log is **in memory only**, bounded to the last 100 entries. It is
deliberately not written to disk: a file that can silently fail to appear is
worse than no file at all.

`testToast` reporting `delivered: true` only means a `Notification` was
constructed. To confirm it reached the operating system, compare Windows' own
record for this app's AUMID before and after:

```powershell
$k = 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Notifications\Settings\electron.app.DeepSeek Harness'
[DateTime]::FromFileTime([int64](Get-ItemProperty $k).LastNotificationAddedTime)
```

This is how the plugin was verified: the timestamp held steady across a 12-second
idle control, then advanced on each `testToast`.

```bash
node --check index.js
node --check client.js
node test/watcher.test.mjs
```

The test loads `client.js` under a fake `__ModuleLoader__`, feeds it synthetic
Session-status transitions, and asserts which toasts fire and what the decision
log records. It exits non-zero on failure.

**Keep `dependencies` empty.** The desktop profile installs this package with
pnpm's `link:` protocol, and pnpm does not install a linked package's own
dependencies. Declaring one would make dependency resolution fail during Cordis
tree initialisation and stop DSH from starting.
